verdicts.note: Refers to herself among the 7 girls on the course; female confirmed.
Aero with auto as sister discipline = Aeronautical & Automotive dept.
'2 years' in plus 'last year' references are consistent with Year 2; inferential but ok.
'found it quite interesting' supports agree on interesting work.
'good basis for anything... you can go wherever' supports maths/sci without specialising.
'good basis for anything afterwards' directly supports good-degree-regardless.
'taking stuff apart and building things' = technical hobbies; supports agree.
'didn't really know about it till I got here' supports little prior knowledge.
Grandfathers engineers but 'learnt afterwards' = did not know via family; disagree correct.
Parents bemused ('engineer, really?'); no maternal encouragement; disagree.
'mum and dad... engineer, really?' = no paternal encouragement; disagree.
Teachers not enthusiastic, pushed toward teaching; disagree on encouragement.
School staff not enthusiastic about engineering; no careers encouragement; disagree.
Pushed toward teaching away from engineering = redirection/discouragement; borderline but ok.
Those who redirected were school teachers; consistent with teacher(s).
'thought there'd be more building' = practical level not just right; disagree.
On-balance pleased; corroborated by 'happy with career choices'; cited quote conditional but agree holds.
'they know your name, more personal' leans to females getting more attention but is about being known, not help; thin -> low.
'pulls their weight' is about group-work effort, not student competitiveness; does not address the variable.
'help each other' via group work supports course developing interpersonal skills.
'he's been great... really good... everybody's encouraging' = satisfied with lecturer support.
Barely seen tutor, wants someone else; clearly dissatisfied.
'rather do group work than individual any day' = very satisfied.
'fantastic 2 weeks... building it' = very satisfied with practical work.
'opened my eyes to loads more subjects' supports satisfaction with variety.
Whinges about amount of lectures vs other courses; supports dissatisfaction with teaching hours.
Decided not to go; 'get a degree over and then start working'; no confirmed.
'if I take a year out I won't get back into education' directly supports break-fear reason.
'get a degree over and then start working' plus 'wanting the money' supports finish-uni-to-earn.
Only non-engineering summer work; never cited as reason; disagree by inference, thin -> low.
'gone into design... like for a car' supports design work as preferred area.
'probably management – management sounds good' supports managerial, though tentative.
'Best things – money' plus coy admissions; important (not very) is well calibrated.
Names location/close-to-home first and repeatedly; very important supported.
Cited quote is about job security/staying, not promotion per se; loose match -> downgrade to low.
Term prompted by interviewer but she affirms substantively ('training would be good, opportunities afterwards').
Concept supplied entirely by interviewer's list; bare echo 'yeah'; interviewer-planted, reject.
'not that big on travelling' supports travel being unimportant.
'free cars' is a jokey dream-job aside, not a stated job-decision factor; does not support importance of benefits.
Orients to working not further study; never mentions postgrad; 'no' supported by inference, low confidence apt.
